html:
The Tenharim are a Kawahib people of the southern Amazon in the Brazilian state of Amazonas, living along the Marmelos River, a tributary of the Madeira. They speak a Tupi-Guarani language close to that of the Parintintin and the Jiahui.

Rubber tappers entered their land in the early 1900s and brought disease. In the 1970s the Trans-Amazonian Highway was built straight through their territory, and settlers and loggers followed. The tribe later charged a toll on the road through their land, which caused clashes with the people of the nearby town of Humaitá in 2013. Today the Tenharim number about a thousand.
